html:
Songtsen Gampo was the king who founded the Tibetan Empire in the 7th century. He ruled from about 618 or 629 until his death in 650; his birth date is not certain.

He inherited a kingdom in the Yarlung valley and united the tribes of the Tibetan plateau into one power. He moved his capital to Lhasa and conquered neighbouring lands, probably including Zhangzhung to the west.

He made alliances by marriage. One queen was Bhrikuti, a princess from Nepal. Another was Princess Wencheng, sent by the emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty in 641 after Tibetan armies pressed on China's border.

Later Tibetan tradition makes him the first of the three "Dharma Kings":

  • He is said to have brought Buddhism to Tibet, with help from his two queens.
  • He built the Jokhang temple in Lhasa.
  • He sent the minister Thonmi Sambhota to India to create the Tibetan script.
  • He is credited with Tibet's first law code.

How much of this is true is hard to say, since most accounts were written centuries later. But the empire he founded was a great power of Asia for two hundred years.
sum: Songtsen Gampo was the king who founded the Tibetan Empire in the 7th century. He ruled from about 618 or 629 until his death in 650; his birth date is not certain.
